structure.title: Love made public
structure.text: Lear's division of the kingdom turns familial speech into a test with political consequences. Gloucester's household introduces a parallel disturbance.

structure.title: Authority stripped and tested
structure.text: Journeys through households and exposed landscapes test what remains of loyalty when status no longer secures obedience.

people.name: Gloucester
people.text: A nobleman facing conflict within his own family.

context.title: Power and dependence
context.text: Giving away government does not erase the need for shelter, service, or affection. Lear tries to preserve expectations after changing their basis.

context.title: Parallel households
context.text: The two family plots echo one another without being identical. Comparisons expose different forms of misjudgment and loyalty.

opening: Lear offers his daughters portions of his kingdom according to how extravagantly they declare their love. He wants to give up the work of ruling while keeping the deference, comfort, and authority. One daughter refuses to perform the speech he expects. The consequences spread from a family ceremony into a country where people must choose between telling the truth and remaining safe. Shakespeare strips an old king of the arrangements that made him feel loved, leaving others to discover what they owe him without the crown.
